article.headline: From Manifesto to Mini-App: Andreessen Demos His Own Build Thesis
article.lede: In April 2020, Marc Andreessen published 'It's Time to Build,' a widely circulated essay arguing that Western societies had stagnated through an unwillingness to create. Six years later, in a single tweet, he offered a demonstration of what he believes has changed: a plain-English prompt, sent to an AI app-builder, is now sufficient to commission working software. The implication is that the barrier separating an idea from a product has effectively collapsed.
article.body:
The tweet performs a recursive loop. By opening with 'It's time to build' — the title of his 2020 essay — and then immediately issuing a natural-language directive to @Wabi, Andreessen stages a live proof of his own argument. The update to the thesis sits in the next five words: 'now everyone can.' The friction that once confined software creation to engineers has, the tweet implies, been engineered away.

**Wabi** was founded by Eugenia Kuyda, who previously built *Replika*, an AI companionship app that amassed 40 million users. In November 2025 the company raised $20 million in pre-seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), the firm Andreessen co-founded. Wabi positions itself as a *user-generated software* platform: a user describes an app in a sentence, and the system handles icon design, database setup, and interface layout automatically, then publishes the result to a shared social graph. Andreessen Horowitz has compared the model to what Alphabet (GOOGL)'s YouTube did for video — anyone can now not just distribute software but create it.

Readers should note that Andreessen is endorsing a company his own firm funded. The tweet functions simultaneously as manifesto and portfolio promotion. That does not invalidate the broader thesis, which has wide industry support, but it supplies the commercial context for the demonstration.

The specific app Andreessen commissions — one that recommends films and novels with **techno-optimist** themes — ties the demo to his October 2023 essay of the same name: a 5,200-word argument that technological progress is the primary driver of human well-being and must be accelerated rather than constrained. The requested app is also an artefact: software designed to propagate a worldview that, by Andreessen's own live demonstration, anyone can now instantiate in minutes.

concepts.definition: The belief that technological progress is the primary driver of human well-being, and that societies should actively accelerate — rather than restrain — technological development. Andreessen formalized his version in a 5,200-word October 2023 manifesto, which frames skepticism of technology as the principal threat to human flourishing.

A category of software creation in which non-technical users produce functional applications via natural-language prompts rather than code. Analogous to user-generated content on video platforms, UGS platforms handle all underlying technical infrastructure — databases, UI, hosting — automatically. The term is closely associated with Wabi's product positioning.

The earliest formal round of venture capital investment, typically raised before a product has launched at scale or demonstrated commercial traction. It is used to fund initial product development and team-building, and usually comes from a single lead investor alongside angels.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.

poster_pmarca.blurb: Marc Andreessen is a co-founder of Andreessen Horowitz, one of the most influential venture capital firms in Silicon Valley. He is a prolific poster on X, sharing insights on technology, startups, crypto, and macroeconomics. With over 1.5 million followers, his tweets often spark debate and are widely shared across the tech and finance communities.
poster_pmarca.credibility_note: Andreessen is a highly credible figure in tech and venture capital, but his strong opinions on crypto and politics have drawn criticism. He has been known to promote projects his firm has invested in without always disclosing conflicts.
